title: NewTimesheet
role: Imaginatto — Software Development Intern, Full Stack
description: Timesheet management system built for Imaginatto in PHP with the CodeIgniter framework, replacing their legacy timesheet with a newly modelled database and business rules.
extendedDescription: This was my first ever real-life project, taken on as a software development intern. My job was renewing Imaginatto's timesheet system end to end: modelling the new database and coding the business rules in PHP with CodeIgniter, while primarily working under the supervision of the senior developers. I worked across the full stack — the back-end in PHP/CodeIgniter and the front-end built with Bootstrap. The system went on to be used company-wide for years after it was built.

title: Framework Alpha
description: PHP framework built for AM4 to standardise development across the company's web systems and webservices, packed with the shared code and functions used most often.
extendedDescription: Built together with another developer, this was a from-scratch PHP framework meant to speed up and standardise development across AM4 — reusable functions, patterns and boilerplate that the two of us, and later the rest of the team, relied on across a lot of projects afterwards. It was completely back-end, with no interface of its own, purely there to make everyday coding easier across the company's PHP projects.

title: ProgrammerTime
url: Estácio de Sá University — final year thesis (TCC)
role: Personal Project — Final Year Thesis (TCC), Full Stack
description: ProgrammerTime® is an internal management tool for software development companies to control projects, tasks, clients and employees in real time — built as my final year thesis at Estácio de Sá University.
extendedDescription: Built together with a course partner as our final thesis (TCC), scoring 10/10. ProgrammerTime® helps small, medium and large companies control their projects, tasks, clients and employees anywhere in real time, and was later adopted for real use by companies in Rio de Janeiro.

title: Immunotech
description: Multi-tenant clinical management system built solo at SCE Sistemas for allergology and dermatology clinics running patch and prick tests, in partnership with FDA Allergenic's PatchKit Standard line.
extendedDescription: Immunotech manages the full patch/prick test lifecycle for clinics — patient and physician registration, test scheduling with dual reading windows (48h/96h readings per substance), reaction recording, and automatic PDF report generation. It's multi-tenant: each clinic's data is isolated, and access is gated by a per-clinic subscription plan with report-count quotas and validity windows that auto-deactivate accounts on expiry, enforced at login rather than through a static flag. Years after the original build, I revisited the ~2015 codebase to get it running on PHP 8, including tracking down a subtle CodeIgniter 3 session-cookie incompatibility (CI3 validates session IDs against PHP's old 40-char SHA1 format, which breaks on PHP 7.1+'s shorter default session ID format).

title: Jurídico
url: SCE Sistemas — legal case management system
description: Legal case/demand management system built solo at SCE Sistemas for a law office, tracking legal processes, the tasks and hearings requested on them, outside correspondents, clients and per-comarca billing, split across a staff hub and a client portal.
extendedDescription: Jurídico is a pair of sibling CodeIgniter applications sharing one database: the internal staff hub, where coordinators manage clients, correspondents, processes, demands, pricing tables and reports; and a client-facing portal where clients log in to open new demands, track status and exchange files on their own cases. Years after the original ~2016 build, I revisited the codebase to get it running on PHP 8.1, fixing raw SQL queries that concatenated user input directly (notably the login query and the demand search/filter screens) to use parameter binding and integer casting instead.

title: SimMed
description: Clinical case simulator built solo at SCE Sistemas for medical and health students, letting instructors script cases with costed vitals, labs and imaging while students order tests and submit diagnoses and treatment plans.
extendedDescription: SimMed lets instructors build clinical cases with associated variables — vitals, labs, imaging — each carrying a cost and a scripted outcome, while students work the case by ordering the variables they think are relevant and submitting their own diagnosis and treatment plan. Years after the original ~2016 build, I revisited the codebase after it was inherited in a broken state: fixed PHP 8 compatibility issues and patched CodeIgniter 3 core incompatibilities with modern PHP, replaced plaintext password storage with password_hash()/password_verify(), converted raw SQL queries to bound parameters to close SQL injection holes, added open-redirect protection, moved credentials into a gitignored .env file, and reconstructed the database schema from the model queries.
